text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to settle onboarding acceptance for the new model cohort. proposal: require 2 benchmark suites (latency P50/P95 + quality eval) OR allow 1 suite + provisional pin for 30 days. thoughts?
ben: leaning toward 2 full suites. provisional pins add churn and hidden cost.
kai: customer asks keep coming for faster onboarding. can we do 1 suite + canary traffic (5%) and strict telemetry?
sophie: if we go provisional pin route we should define automatic rollback triggers. suggest: quality drop >3% on core prompts OR error rate >0.5% for 24h => auto-unpin.
maria: agree on rollback triggers. need to decide whether provisional pins count against SLA for Dedicated customers. That was a big ask from sales.
ben: Dedicated customers expect stable pinned versions. provisional pins should be flagged as "experimental" and excluded from SLA guarantees. Addline to contract? @kai?
kai: yeah we can add contract language. ops-bot: Reminder: catalog config requires a `pin_state` enum: ["pinned","provisional","unpinned"]. Add rollout metadata: `canary_fraction`,`start_ts`,`rollback_triggers`.
sophie: also add a gating checklist for onboarding: 1) infra perf benchmark (P95 < target), 2) quality eval run (n=200 prompts, pass rate >= threshold), 3) model card + known failure modes documented, 4) privacy/KMS check clear.
maria: i put an initial draft of checklist into the doc: https://redwood.docs/cat/onboard-checklist (WIP). want Product approval before we publish.
ben: timing: can we pilot this with 2 non-enterprise models next sprint? if pilot passes, roll to general onboarding.
kai: pilot ok but set canary_fraction = 0.05 and auto-escalation to oncall if any of the rollback triggers fire.
sophie: for metrics, we'll surface: token-cost delta, latency delta (baseline), quality regression %, and customer error surface. add them to console dashboard.
maria: question about deprecation windows: how long should we give customers after a pinned model is retired? proposal: 90 days for general, 180 days for enterprise committed customers.
ben: 90/180 seems fine. add opt-in migration assistance for enterprise during the 180 window.
kai: we need migration runbooks for common adapters (tokenizer shims, config diffs). CTO wants a 'zero-surprise' checklist for migrations.
sophie: launch criteria summary for this policy: - onboarding checklist green - pilot run 2 models with no rollbacks for 14d - console telemetry added - contract language approved.
maria: ok i'll align with legal and sales on contract text, ops to add `pin_state` + rollback rules, eng to build canary plumbing. assigning owners in the doc.
ben: small nit — include a "grace pin" mode for critical customers who explicitly accept higher cost/risk during migration. must be opt-in and logged.
kai: agreed. we'll also provide a migration SLA (response time & runbook support) as a paid add-on.
maria: cool. i'll spin a public RFC draft tomorrow and tag everyone. any last asks?
sophie: add a short section about model-variant compatibility (tokenizer/embedding dims) to reduce migration surprises.
ben: +1. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deploy note: added feature flag `catalog.provisional_pins` scoped to product team. Toggle in Console -> Feature Flags."
